characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: D/MAX-2500/PC XRD with Cu Kα X-ray tube (ASTM: D5380–93[2014])
characterization_methods.key_findings: Rolled 0Be steel consists of austenite and carbide; its XRD trace shows the γ reflections (111) ≈43° and (200) ≈50° plus weaker reflections near 65°, 74°, 86° and 91°, with no δ or Be-compound markers.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Polished specimen, 2θ range 20°–100°, scanning speed 2°/min, continuous scanning; rolled (1050 °C) strip
characterization_methods.purpose: Phase composition of the rolled steel

characterization_methods.key_findings: 0Be rolled shows a γ-Fe matrix with dark needle-like/platelet precipitates aligned along deformation bands and faint needle structure; two red circles/ellipse mark annealing twins.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Rolled strips, RD–ND plane, etched with 8% nitrate alcohol solution; 50 µm scale bars

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: EBSD coupled with Hitachi S3400 SEM; TSL OIM analysis v8 software
characterization_methods.key_findings: 0Be rolled phase map is almost entirely green (austenite) with no resolvable red ferrite; KAM map predominantly deep blue with sparse green/yellow hot-spots (least misorientation of the series); grain size ~55% in the range 12–18 μm (Fig. 14a).
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: RD–ND plane, electropolished at -20 °C for 50–65 s at 20 V in electrolyte of perchloric acid (HClO4) and alcohol (C2H6O), ratio 1:9
characterization_methods.purpose: Microstructure, grain boundary, KAM and phase analysis

characterization_methods.key_findings: Matrix is austenite (γ-Fe, zone axis [1̄14], spots 022, 311, 3̄11); precipitates in 0Be are κ-carbide (zone axis [001], spots 010, 110, 100).
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Sample thinned to 40 μm with waterproof sand paper, then electrochemical polishing with a dual jet in 10% perchloric acid with 90% ethanol at 26.5 V and -20 °C
characterization_methods.purpose: Identify the matrix and precipitate phases in the rolled steel
characterization_methods.technique: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) and selected-area diffraction (SAED)

characterization_methods.key_findings: The 0Be fracture surface is dominated by a rough ductile fibrous zone densely covered with dimples; spherical inclusions are evident in the dimples of area A1, and dissociation planes and river patterns appear in the macro fracture area A2.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Tensile fracture surfaces of rolled specimens; 0Be panel has a 25 µm scale bar
Tap of 500 gf force; each sample tested using a 15×5 matrix, average value of 25 points

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Instron 5982 universal tester and dynamic extensometer (Instron 2620–601)
characterization_methods.key_findings: Rolled 0Be: YS 989.51 MPa, UST 1222.27 MPa, TE 22.91%.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Room temperature, initial strain rate 5 × 10^-4 m·s^-1, ASTM E8/E8M-16A; specimens machined from the rolled sheet
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure tensile properties of the rolled steel

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Deionised water (ρ = 1 × 10^3 g/cm³); average density from three independently measured values per sample
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure the density of the experimental steel

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Fe–Be binary alloy, temperature 0–1800 °C, composition axis Fe/(Be+Fe) = 0–1 (mol/mol); line compounds FeBe12 (≈0.13), FeBe5 (≈0.17) and FeBe2 (≈0.33) with invariant lines near 1150, 1050 and 680 °C

analytical_models.equation_role: Calculate the density of the experimental steel from measured masses
analytical_models.model_note: V0 = (m1 − m2)/ρ_water (Eq. 1) gives the volume of displaced deionised water; ρ0 = m0/V0 (Eq. 2) gives the density of the steel.

analytical_models.equation_role: Determine the solid solution type from atomic radii of solvent and solute
analytical_models.model_note: Δr = |(r_A − r_B)/r_A| (Eq. 3). When Δr < 8% and crystal structures match an infinite solid solution forms; Be forms a substitutional solid solution in the Fe matrix.

defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: Some annealing twins are observed in the rolled microstructure of the 0Be steel (Fig. 8a, Fig. 17a).

interfaces.phase_evolution: Rolled 0Be remains a single austenite (γ) phase matrix with κ-carbide precipitates; no ferrite forms in the absence of Be addition, in contrast to the 1.0Be/1.5Be dual-phase (γ + δ) steels.
interfaces.slip_behavior: Under the action of external force, a large number of dislocation slip movements and accumulation occur inside the steel.

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Alloys made from high-purity elements Fe (99.99%), Mn (99.99%), Al (99.99%) and C (99.99%) and melted into alloy ingots; obtained ingot has a diameter of 60 mm and a thickness of 30 mm. This is the as-cast precursor (proc_as-cast) of the rolled sample.
Plate of 5 mm thickness obtained by 17 times hot rolling with two-high mill rolls at 1050 °C (1.5 mm per roll, strain rate of 0.6 s^-1), equivalent to 83% of the total deformation.
processing_steps.reduction_ratio: 83% total deformation (17 passes, 1.5 mm per pass)

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: After each rolling pass, the sample was kept in a muffle furnace for 3 min to maintain the rolling temperature.
After the last pass of rolling, water cooling was performed until cooled to room temperature.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Each experimental data supported by more than three tensile specimens; microhardness measured with FM-ARS9000 Vickers tester at 500 gf (15×5 matrix, average of 25 points); density determined by Archimedes drainage as the average of three independent measurements
measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: flat tensile specimen (dimensions 50, 20, 10, 6, 3 and R5; obtained by electric discharge machining/wire cutting from the rolled sheet)
measurement_conditions.strain_rate: 5 × 10^-4 m·s^-1 (initial strain rate for tensile tests)

tensile_properties.strain_hardening_rate: Fig. 10(b): strain hardening rate dσ/dε vs true strain for 0Be falls steeply from above the 5 GPa axis limit to a steady-state plateau between roughly 1.3 and 2.2 GPa; the 0Be curve lies between the 0.5Be (lowest) and 1.5Be (highest) curves.
tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Fig. 10(a): engineering stress–strain curve of rolled 0Be (black) reaches the highest engineering stress of the series (peaking between the 1200 and 1300 MPa gridlines) and drops abruptly a little after 20% strain.

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: Fig. 14(a): grain size of 0Be is approximately 55% in the range 12–18 μm; unimodal distribution with tallest bar centred on 15 μm, secondary shoulder at 18 μm and a tail extending to 30 μm.

phases_present.morphology: equiaxed grains with banded deformation structure

precipitates.distribution: present within the matrix (stress concentration on the carbide evident in KAM); coarse carbide particle observed by TEM

structures.overall_structure: Rolled 0Be steel consists of austenite and carbide; the microstructure is a single-phase austenite (γ) matrix with κ-carbide precipitates, retaining a banded deformation structure and annealing twins, with no ferrite resolvable by XRD or EBSD.

unmapped_findings: Rolled 0Be tensile fracture surface is fully ductile: a rough fibrous zone densely covered with dimples, with spherical inclusions evident in the dimples (Area A1) and dissociation planes/river patterns in the macro fracture region A2 (Fig. 12). With increasing Be content the dimples decrease and cleavage platforms appear, so only 0Be is purely ductile.
Among the rolled series, 0Be steel reaches the highest engineering stress (peak between the 1200 and 1300 MPa gridlines) and fails a little after 20% strain (Fig. 10a).

DSC transformation temperature of the Be-free alloy: the text states 1278.8 °C while the printed peak label in Fig. 6 reads 1320 °C (broad peak rising from ~1270 °C). After adding Be the transformation point dropped by approximately 120 °C (0.5Be = 1165.9 °C, 1.0Be = 1163.3 °C, 1.5Be = 1154.8 °C).

The Ashby plot of strength–ductility product vs density (Fig. 20) includes only the 0.5Be, 1.0Be and 1.5Be Be-steels, not the 0Be alloy; the Be-steel family is reported as ~21.38% lower in density than pure iron.

The 0Be alloy is the series reference: without Be addition it forms no Be–Fe phase (no reticular or Chinese-character compounds), and its rolled structure is single-phase austenite with κ-carbide, whereas the Be-bearing steels develop a banded γ + δ dual-phase structure with dispersed Be–Fe phase precipitates.
